title: How well do fast discrete trigonometric transforms work for parametric numerical integration?
summary: The fast Fourier transform (FFT) and its real counterparts, the fast algorithms of the discrete cosine transform (DCT) and the discrete sine transform (DST), are frequently employed for the numerical evaluation of the Fourier cosine and Fourier sine transform, thereby acting as parametric quadrature rules based on finitely many samples of a given continuous function. But how accurate are the obtained results? In this paper we study the error occurring if the DCT of type I (DCT-I) and the DST of type I (DST-I) are applied to compute $\int_0^{\infty} f(x)\cos(2πxv)\d x$ and $\int_0^{\infty}…
